pageKinds.description: A create/read/update/delete page over a single repository.
A read-only search/list page (照会). Search + table, no form.
A master-maintenance page. Same shape as crud (search + table + form).
A read-only single-record detail page. Displays the form's fields.
A standalone create/edit form page (form only, no table).
A stepped-input page: the form is split into steps, each validated on its own before advancing. Persisted once, on the final step.

A dashboard page: a grid of read-only cards, each one a small query plus how to display its result. It addresses no single record, so it has no `key`, and `repository` is only the default for cards that declare none.

A report page (帳票): read-only rows laid out on sheets, grouped with subtotals — the printable counterpart of a list. Detail columns come from `table`; `report` adds only the printing structure. It addresses no single record, so it has no `key`.

keys.description: Action type (open string). Built-ins: create, edit, delete, navigate, plugin, export, print.
What the action runs on. 'page' (default) acts on the screen; 'selection' acts on the rows the user checked, and makes the table selectable.
Registered action plugin key (used when type is 'plugin').
Target page id (used when type is 'navigate').
Route params for a navigate action; $row.id / $record.id template against the current row/record.

Ask before running the action. A `delete` action asks even without this; declaring it replaces the wording. `title` and `message` may carry `{count}`, the number of rows picked — filled only on a `scope: selection` action, since nothing else knows a count before it runs. Nothing has happened yet, so `{failed}` / `{total}` / `{error}` do not fill here (`validate` says so).
What happens once the action succeeded. Nothing here runs when it fails.
What the user is told when the action failed. Placeholders: {error} the reason as reported, {failed} / {count} / {total} the row counts of a `scope: selection` action.

Asked before the action runs: a small form whose values reach the handler as `input`. It replaces the confirmation dialog rather than adding a second one — the same OK button confirms. `title` may carry `{count}` on a `scope: selection` action. Style the OK button as destructive with `confirm: { danger: true }` (the prompt has no `danger` of its own).

For `scope: selection`: how many rows one press may act on. A plain integer caps everyone; the object form caps per role. While more than the limit are picked the button is disabled and says the limit — it never truncates the selection, since acting on part of what was picked is the failure nobody notices. Omit to leave it unbounded, in which case the real limit is how many rows are on screen (`table.pagination.pageSize`).
Plugin / renderer specific extra settings.

Enabled only while this condition matches. The record judged is the row for a row action, every checked row for scope: selection (all of them must match), and the current record for a page that has one. A page with no record to judge leaves the button enabled (validate says so).
Roles allowed to see this item/action. Empty or absent = everyone. UI-level display gating only, not access enforcement.

action.params.description: Route params for a navigate action; $row.id / $record.id template against the current row/record.

actionError.description: What the user is told when the action failed. Placeholders: {error} the reason as reported, {failed} / {count} / {total} the row counts of a `scope: selection` action.

keys.description: Shown instead of the raw failure (a snackbar / toast).

Style the OK button as destructive with `confirm: { danger: true }` (the prompt has no `danger` of its own).

keys.description: Dialog heading. Defaults to the action's label.
Confirming button. Falls back to `confirm.okLabel`, then the label.
Cancelling button. Falls back to `confirm.cancelLabel`.
What to ask. Ordinary fields: types, required, validators, computed and normalize behave as in a form.

actionSuccess.description: What happens once the action succeeded. Nothing here runs when it fails.

keys.description: Shown briefly to the user (a snackbar / toast).
Page id to move to afterwards.
Route params for `page`; $row.id / $record.id template against the current row/record.

condition.description: A conditional expression evaluated against a record. Either a leaf {field, operator, value}, a leaf {mode: create|edit}, or a combinator {all|any: [..]} / {not: {..}}.

keys.description: True while the form is in this mode. Use it for "only when creating" / "only when editing" instead of inspecting the key field. False wherever the mode is unknown (a read-only detail page has none).
Built-ins: equals, notEquals, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, in, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
A conditional expression evaluated against a record. Either a leaf {field, operator, value}, a leaf {mode: create|edit}, or a combinator {all|any: [..]} / {not: {..}}.

document.description: A hatake document: either a single `page` or an `app` (pages + navigation).

keys.description: DSL version the document conforms to.
An application: pages composed by a navigation menu.
Field type (open string). Built-ins: text, textarea, number, select, multiSelect, checkbox, radio, date, dateTime, time, subTable. A subTable holds child rows — see columns / fields / source.
Required only when the condition matches the current record. Unlike visibleWhen / enabledWhen this is also checked server-side, by the same validator.
Read-only while the condition matches: the value stays readable, only editing is blocked. Compare enabledWhen, which greys the input out.
Value applied when creating a new record.
Parent field name. The options shown are those whose `when` matches the parent's current value (plus any option without a `when`). Changing the parent clears a child value that is no longer offered.

Fetch a field's options from a repository instead of listing them. The framework knows no HTTP or SQL: it asks the repository the application registered, passing the parent value as a filter when `parentKey` is set.
Display formatter name (open string). Built-ins: currency, percent, date, wareki, postal, mask.
Input converters applied before validation. Built-ins: toHankaku, toZenkaku, hiraToKata, kataToHira, trim, collapseSpaces, parseNumber.
Plugin / renderer specific extra settings.
Show this field only when the condition matches the current record.
Enable this field only when the condition matches the current record. A disabled field is greyed out; use readOnlyWhen when the value should stay plainly readable.

Derive the field value from the record. Two modes: `fields` folds values of the same record (concat / sum / subtract / product), while `field` folds the rows of a subTable (count / sum / avg / min / max — the same aggregate vocabulary as dashboards and `compare` — plus `join`, which lists the rows as one string). Row-folding accepts `where` to keep only some rows. Derived once, in declaration order. Extensible via ComputedRegistry.
Roles allowed to see this item/action. Empty or absent = everyone. UI-level display gating only, not access enforcement.
Child-row grid columns, for type: subTable (master-detail). The field's value is then a list of records.
Editor fields for one child row, for type: subTable. Omit to derive inputs from `columns`.

Fetch a subTable's child rows from their own repository, paged and linked by a foreign key, instead of embedding them in the parent record. Rows are then saved per row (create/update/delete) and require the parent to already have a key.

field.computed.description: Derive the field value from the record. Two modes: `fields` folds values of the same record (concat / sum / subtract / product), while `field` folds the rows of a subTable (count / sum / avg / min / max — the same aggregate vocabulary as dashboards and `compare` — plus `join`, which lists the rows as one string). Row-folding accepts `where` to keep only some rows. Derived once, in declaration order. Extensible via ComputedRegistry.

keys.description: Same-record ops: concat, sum, subtract, product (with `fields`). Row-folding ops: count, sum, avg, min, max, join (with `field`). Open string — register your own on ComputedRegistry.
Fields of the same record to fold (same-record mode).
A `subTable` field of this form whose rows are folded (row-folding mode). The rows must be saved with the parent record: a subTable with `source` is paged, so its rows are not here to fold.
Which value of each row to fold. Required except for `count`. Same meaning as `of` on the `compare` validator.

Row-folding mode only: fold just the rows matching this condition, evaluated against one row (the same condition language as `visibleWhen`). `{ mode: ... }` is never true here — a row has no form mode.
What goes between the joined values. Default: empty for `concat` (it packs values of one record, like a name), ", " for `join` (it lists rows, which are unreadable packed together).
Backing data key.
Input type (open string). Built-ins: text, textarea, number, select, multiSelect, checkbox, radio, date, dateTime, time.
Match operator (open string). Built-ins: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, endsWith, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in.
Options for select-style filters.

Parent filter name in the same search area. The options shown are those whose `when` matches the parent's current value (plus any option without a `when`). Changing the parent clears a child value that is no longer offered.

Fetch a field's options from a repository instead of listing them. The framework knows no HTTP or SQL: it asks the repository the application registered, passing the parent value as a filter when `parentKey` is set.
Plugin / renderer specific extra settings.

validator.description: A validation rule. 'type' selects the validator; remaining keys (except 'message') are passed as parameters: maxLength / minLength / min / max take 'value', pattern takes 'pattern', and compare takes 'operator' (equals / notEquals / gt / gte / lt / lte) plus 'field' (the field to compare with), optionally 'aggregate' + 'of' to fold a subTable into a number, and 'where' to fold only some of its rows (the same row filter as `computed`).

keys.description: Validator type (open string). Built-ins: required, maxLength, minLength, pattern, min, max, email, postalCode, compare. compare is the cross-field one: it reads another field of the same record (see the node description for its parameters).
Override message shown on failure.
